-110.94600,32.33440.name: Arizona Reproductive Institute
-110.94600,32.33440.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

2.17707,41.38258.name: Institut d'Investigació Biomedica de Bellvitge (IDIBELL)
2.17707,41.38258.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-73.55965,45.57485.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, May 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-97.74300,30.26700.name: Colossal — Form Bio spin-out
-97.74300,30.26700.desc: Colossal’s computational platform, spun out as its own company and sold to other biotechnology firms. It shows what the de-extinction business is actually built on: the mammoth raises the money and generates the coverage, and the software, enzymes and methods developed along the way are the products with buyers.

32.85970,39.93340.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (Türkiye) — biosafety board
32.85970,39.93340.desc: Turkey prohibits the cultivation of engineered crops and permits their import for animal feed, with a biosafety board approving specific events for that purpose. The prohibition and the imports coexist because the political objection attaches to growing rather than to eating, which is a distinction most national debates end up making somewhere.

-0.12480,51.49950.name: Home Office — licensed establishments
-0.12480,51.49950.desc: Every UK establishment licensed to use animals in research holds a licence from the Home Office, and every procedure is counted and published in annual statistics. What is not published is which establishment did what: the numbers are national, the names are withheld, so British laboratories cannot be mapped while British fertility clinics can.

-96.79840,44.31140.name: Medgene
-96.79840,44.31140.desc: A company built around a regulatory category rather than a product. In 2018 the US Department of Agriculture created a pathway allowing a vaccine PLATFORM to be licensed rather than each vaccine made on it, and Medgene's business is that pathway: it holds licences for prescription platform vaccines in cattle — influenza D, coronavirus, rotavirus, papillomavirus — and has produced them for swine, rabbits and deer, with a veterinarian required to prescribe and supervise each use. Because the platform was already approved in cattle it could move quickly on an H5N1 vaccine for dairy herds during the fourth year of the outbreak, reaching final review for conditional licence and a distribution agreement with one of the largest animal health companies. This is the most consequential regulatory idea in the facet: approve the method once and the organisms made on it need only a shorter review, which is what makes a rapid response possible and what makes the register of approved products stop describing what is actually in use.
